pages.lesson:
LESSON: RHYTHM AND PATTERN MAKING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.4: Rhythm and Pattern Making

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Rhythm and Pattern Making. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why create rhythm in different beat patterns?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. compose a rhythm using a combination of musical notes and their rests

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: RHYTHM AND PATTERN MAKING
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Rhythm and Pattern Making helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

PART 1: Compose a rhythm using a combination of musical notes and their rests

What this means
In this part you learn to compose a rhythm using a combination of musical notes and their rests. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: compose a rhythm using a combination of musical notes and their rests.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Rhythm and Pattern Making” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can compose a rhythm using a combination of musical notes and their rests. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Rhythm and Pattern Making is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Rhythm and Pattern Making” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: compose a rhythm using a combination of musical notes and their rests)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Rhythm and Pattern Making to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: compose a rhythm using a combination of musical notes and their rests.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Rhythm and Pattern Making from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Rhythm and Pattern Making: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Rhythm and Pattern Making?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why create rhythm in different beat patterns?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Rhythm and Pattern Making means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: compose a rhythm using a combination of musical notes and their rests.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
